items.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: In fact I was talking to Howard about it.

ctx.x: So you think the future of jazz — it still has a future?

My feeling is everybody says at these jazz parties everybody’s white haired in the audience and everything, and do you think there’s a future, and I say well I think if we’re lucky we’ll all die off at the same time. And it will all go with the audience. But then Harry says well thanks a lot. And I actually sometimes, I don’t know, I mean people say that but I’m glad I’m at the age I am. I don’t think I’d want to be 25 and liking the music © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

that I like and trying to make a living at it. I’m a pessimist enough to think that if Frank Sinatra were starting out singing now, he’d have a hell of a time getting a job, because of the climate of the times and the kind of music that’s popular. So I don’t know. All I know is I’m 52 and maybe I could eke out a living for another 25 years. But I mean certainly it’s going on in the schools, which I think there’s a pro and con to that. I think that like classical music, when it got institutionalized, I don’t think…
